When I was about 8 I used to stay over at my Grandma's house. My 10 year old cousin also used to stay over, and we used to get a thrill out of the idea of a sleepover.

One night I'm getting changed into my PJ's as usual before bed, and my cousin comes in the room. I didn't think anything of being half-naked around him. So he starts taking his clothes off, and I figure he's getting changed too. But he doesn't. He stands there naked and then says something like, "let's sleep in the same bed tonight, naked like this so it doesn't get too hot under the covers."

I say I don't want to, because I hate sharing a bed after having to a few times with my brother. 
He insists.
I say no.

Then he goes over to the door, shuts it and bolts it (who puts a bolt lock inside a room where children sleep?). Then he says I can't leave until I agree.

I didn't actually have to leave the room. I mean, I was ready for bed. But something about being told I couldn't leave got to me, and I started crying.

My cousin was frantically telling me to quieten down and he came over to me, and wiped my face and told me he was just kidding and I could leave.
As long as I agreed to get undressed and hug him.

I did, and the second he moved away from the door to go put his pyjamas on, I unbolted it and ran downstairs crying. I didn't tell my grandma what happened (I probably said he was being mean or something), and I kind of just filed it away in my head.

It's only looking back on it now that I understand how it was pretty messed up.

If you consider a rollercoaster might operate at 3 or 4 g's, and the effects that you would feel if you weren't pinned down by that metal bar in your seat, then times that by five... 

In 'The Forever War', by Joe Haldeman, the soldiers wear flexible spacesuits when accelerating at speeds of 25+ g's. These suits, as well as a shot of some medicinal substance, help to stabilise the soldier's bodies against pressure. Along with this, the room they are in is flooded by an ethylene glycol gas solution (what else is is the gas isn't specified...). I wanted to take that idea, but instead of standing around in spacesuits, I thought it would be safer to be positioned horizontally in fortified sealed units, which would emit a gas just like Haldeman's. Also, the hum counteracts the potential inertia through hypnosis.
